criteria.reasoning: The memo states Saffron & Sage's sole member is Celeste M. Aldana, links her to Thomas Aldana as his spouse via the shared address and his annual statement, and concludes 'A spouse is a Family Member under the policy, so Mr. Aldana had a Financial Interest in the catering contract ... an actual or possible conflict of interest.'

It names both failures: 'on 2026-01-20 he answered "No" to Question 2 ... although Saffron & Sage had submitted its bid on 2026-01-08', and at the 2026-02-12 meeting 'the minutes record that no director other than Ms. Ramaswamy disclosed anything.'

The memo says the policy required him to 'Leave the meeting ... and not vote (Article III, Sections 2–3)', and that instead 'Mr. Aldana then spoke for Saffron & Sage ("a cut above"), moved to award it the contract, and voted for his own motion.'

The memo says the opposite of the required point: 'Setting his vote aside, a majority of the directors who voted still supported Saffron & Sage, so his participation did not change the result.' The criterion fails a memo that says the motion would have carried without his vote.

It states the board 'rejected the Gala Committee's recommendation of Harborview Provisions, the lowest bid at $52,900, and awarded the contract at $68,400 — $15,500 (29.3%) more.' Both bids and the difference are correct.

The memo finds she disclosed on her annual statement, in writing to the Chair and orally, left the room, and the ten remaining directors approved the lowest bid of $18,250 10–0, concluding 'No action is needed concerning Ms. Ramaswamy.'

The memo concludes Saffron & Sage is not reportable because $71,860 is not 'Over $100,000' and states 'Neither transaction needs to be reported in Schedule L, Part IV.' This is exactly the aggregate-threshold reasoning the criterion fails.
The memo never gives a $39,400 single-transaction threshold; it applies only the rule that a transaction 'is reported when all payments to that person in the year exceed $100,000.'
Although it reaches 'No' for BrightStage, it tests the $18,250 only against the $100,000 aggregate threshold and never against the $39,400 single-transaction threshold, which the criterion requires.

Step 1 says the committee 'informs Mr. Aldana in writing of the basis for its belief that he failed to disclose ... and gives him the opportunity to explain' and that 'No finding about his conduct, and no view about whether the omission was deliberate, should be reached before he has responded.'

Step 4 has the disinterested directors re-review the contract 'under Article III, Sections 3(c) and 3(d)' citing the $52,900 and $55,750 bids and fairness, and says if the Theatre overpaid 'the board must consult legal counsel on whether the payment may be an excess benefit transaction under Internal Revenue Code section 4958 and on recovering the excess', expressly not concluding one occurred.

The memo is addressed to the committee including Thomas Aldana and says 'At its September 3 meeting the full committee should agree the notice,' never stating that he must take no part in the committee's or board's deliberations or votes under Article IV, Section 4.

Step 3 says 'If the board, acting by a majority of the disinterested directors, determines that he failed to disclose, it takes appropriate disciplinary and corrective action', and Step 5 says 'Mr. Aldana files a corrected annual statement within 30 days of the board's determination.'
